title: Important Definitions
outcomes: Define control, power, parent and subsidiary.
Define joint control, joint operations and joint ventures.
Define group, NCI and consolidated and separate statements.

meta.exam_tip: Classify every investee before any computation — the label decides the method.

concepts.title: Control, power, parent and subsidiary
body: Control exists when an investor both has exposure to, or rights over, returns that vary with the investee's performance and can use its power over the investee to affect the size of those returns.
Power means currently held rights that let the investor direct the investee's relevant activities — those that significantly affect its returns.
A parent is an entity that controls at least one other entity; a subsidiary is an entity controlled by another.
concepts.analogy: Power + variable returns + the link between them = control.
concepts.work: Holding 60% of votes usually gives power.

concepts.title: Significant influence and associates
body: Significant influence is the ability to take part in decisions on the investee's financial and operating policies, stopping short of control or joint control.

An associate is an investee over which the investor has significant influence. Holding 20% or more of voting power is presumed to give significant influence, unless clearly shown otherwise; under 20% is presumed not to, unless shown otherwise.
Indicators include board representation, participation in policy-making, material transactions, interchange of managerial personnel and provision of essential technical information.
concepts.analogy: Influence is a seat at the table, not the casting vote.
concepts.work: A 15% holder with a board seat may have significant influence.

concepts.title: Joint control, joint operations and joint ventures
body: A joint arrangement is one that two or more parties control jointly. Joint control is contractually agreed sharing of control, which exists only when decisions on relevant activities need the unanimous agreement of the sharing parties.

A joint operation gives the parties with joint control rights to the arrangement's assets and obligations for its liabilities. A joint venture gives those parties rights to the arrangement's net assets.
A party to a joint arrangement who lacks joint control is accounted for by reference to its actual interest (e.g. its share of assets in a joint operation, or Ind AS 109 / Ind AS 28 for a venture).
concepts.analogy: Joint control needs unanimous consent; then ask: assets and liabilities, or net assets?
concepts.work: A shared pipeline where each party takes its share of capacity is a joint operation.

concepts.title: Group, NCI and statement types
body: A group is a parent together with its subsidiaries. Non-controlling interest (NCI) is the equity in a subsidiary that does not belong, directly or indirectly, to the parent.
Consolidated financial statements present the group's figures as those of one economic entity.

Separate financial statements are those presented by a parent, or by an investor with joint control or significant influence, in which such investments are carried at cost, under Ind AS 109 or by the equity method.
concepts.analogy: NCI is the outside owners' slice of a subsidiary.

illustrations.title: Labelling each investee
illustrations.q: Kite Ltd. holds: 75% of A Ltd. (equity ₹400 crore); 30% of B Ltd. with two board seats; 50% of C Ltd. where all key decisions need both owners' consent and C holds the net assets; 50% of D, an unincorporated arrangement where each party takes its share of output and liabilities; 12% of E Ltd. with no board seat. Classify each and compute NCI in A.

jobs.title: Group structure review
jobs.situation: The client has nine investees with varied holdings and agreements.
steps: Read shareholder agreements for decision rules.
Test control, joint control and significant influence.
jobs.takeaway: Definitions applied correctly decide the accounting method.

mcqs.q: Joint control exists only when decisions on relevant activities require:
options: Unanimous consent of the parties sharing control
mcqs.explain: Unanimity defines joint control. In practice: read the agreement.
mcqs.topic: Joint control, joint operations and joint ventures

mcqs.q: A joint venture gives parties rights to:
options: The net assets of the arrangement
mcqs.explain: Net assets distinguish ventures. In practice: equity method.
mcqs.topic: Joint control, joint operations and joint ventures

mcqs.q: Holding 20% or more of voting power is presumed to give:
mcqs.explain: Rebuttable presumption. In practice: look at indicators.

options: Equity in a subsidiary not attributable to the parent
mcqs.explain: Presented within equity. In practice: 100% − parent's share.

options: Existing rights giving the current ability to direct relevant activities
mcqs.explain: Rights, not their exercise. In practice: potential votes may count.
Associates are outside the group. In practice: equity-accounted.

options: Rights to assets and obligations for liabilities
mcqs.explain: Parties account for their share. In practice: line-by-line share.
mcqs.topic: Joint control, joint operations and joint ventures

mcqs.q: An investee in which a 12% holder has no influence is:
options: A financial asset under Ind AS 109
mcqs.explain: Below 20% with no indicators. In practice: FVTPL or FVOCI.

viva.model: An investor has control when it is exposed to or has rights over variable returns and can use its power over the investee to affect those returns.
The ability to take part in an investee's financial and operating policy decisions without controlling them alone or jointly.

viva.q: Distinguish a joint operation and a joint venture.
viva.model: In a joint operation parties have rights to assets and obligations for liabilities; in a joint venture they have rights to net assets.
The part of a subsidiary's equity owned by outsiders, that is, not attributable directly or indirectly to the parent.
Activities of the investee that significantly affect its returns.

cases.title: Zeal Ltd.
cases.case: Zeal Ltd. holds 55% of P Ltd., 22% of Q Ltd. (but a 60% holder ignores Zeal's views and Zeal has no board seat), 50% of R Ltd. under an agreement requiring unanimous decisions, and 18% of S Ltd. with two of seven board seats.

mcqs.explain: Majority voting power usually gives control. In practice: confirm no other arrangements.

options: Not an associate, as the presumption is rebutted
mcqs.explain: Clear evidence of no influence rebuts 20%. In practice: document evidence.
Unanimity required. In practice: then classify as JO or JV.
mcqs.topic: Joint control, joint operations and joint ventures

mcqs.explain: Board seats can give significant influence below 20%. In practice: equity method.
